data.name: Anadi
data.gender_notes: Anadi is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Anadi is a Sanskrit name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘anad’ which means ‘beginning’ or ‘primordial’. In Hindu mythology, Anadi is often used to refer to the primordial god, Brahma, who is believed to be the creator of the universe. The name Anadi carries the meaning “Beginning, Primordial” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Anadi usually hope their child will grow to embody beginning, primordial and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the eternal beginning and the eternal creator.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anadi total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

This name is deeply rooted in Hindu mythology and stands as a reminder of the importance of creation and the origin of life.
data.spiritual_significance: Anadi holds a significant spiritual meaning as it represents the concept of being beyond the beginning or having no beginning. In Hindu philosophy, this is believed to be a divine quality attributed to the ultimate reality or God. The name Anadi therefore encourages introspection and contemplation on the nature of creation and the eternal self.

historical_references.reference: Anadi is a name for the Hindu deity Vishnu in his unmanifested and infinite form. The term Anadi means 'beginningless' or 'unborn'. Anadi is considered to be the source of all creation and the eternal, unchanging reality that underlies the material world.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient India, around 3rd century BCE to 15th century CE

historical_references.reference: Anadi is also the name of a sage in Hindu mythology, who is said to have lived during the Treta Yuga (second of the four ages of Hindu cosmology). He was a great devotee of Lord Vishnu and is remembered for his deep spiritual understanding and self-realization.
